reasoning_notes.reasoning: With no history, opening at zero earns 20 if C also bids zero (half the labor) and wins outright if C bids above zero.
With identical revenues and costs, undercutting the rival earns positive profit; 10 is a cautious opening bid that leaves room to adapt.
C bid 10 and won all labor; matching 10 secures half the pool at a positive margin, while bidding above 10 reduces profit if C stays at 10.
Matching the rival’s previous zero offer secures half the labor at a profit of 10, equal to last round’s profit while avoiding a lower return from undercutting.
Matching C's repeated 10 bid preserves half the labor and earns 5; bidding higher would reduce profit per unit without evidence C will raise.
Both firms earn the same revenue per unit. Matching 10 preserves a positive margin and avoids giving up labor to a lower offer; the two observed rounds suggest B is willing to match.
Matching C’s repeated 10 bid preserves half the labor and earns 5; undercutting by one would win all labor for 9, but risks a wage response. Continue matching while observing.
B has held at 10 for two rounds. Undercutting by 1 captures the full unit at profit 11; matching yields only 5. A higher wage is unprofitable against B's observed offer.
C has held at 10 for three rounds. Matching preserves the current profitable half-share and is safer than risking a higher wage or losing labor with a lower one.
B has held at 10 for three rounds. Matching preserves a 50% share and earns 5; undercutting to 9 earns 9 but risks a race to the bottom. With an unknown horizon, match and observe.
A has not participated in prior rounds. Matching the established wage of 10 gives a chance at half the labor while preserving 10 profit if tied; undercutting yields less profit per unit.
C has repeatedly bid 10, and matching earns B a profitable half-share. With no known final round, keep the established bid.
B has held at 10 for several rounds; matching preserves a 5 profit while a lower wage risks zero labor and a higher wage earns nothing if B stays.
At 10, matching the established wage yields one-third share and about 3.33 profit; undercutting sacrifices margin, while raising loses all labor if others stay at 10.
Matching the established bid earns a profitable share; undercutting sacrifices margin, while bidding higher risks losing labor at a loss.
Undercutting the tied wage of 10 by one wins the full unit for profit 11, exceeding the 3.33 earned by matching.
Matching 10 preserves half the labor against B’s 10 while C’s 9 earns nothing; a higher wage would cut profit without gaining share.
A and B both bid 10 last round while C bid 9. Matching 10 preserves a profitable half-share if A repeats and beats C; the unknown horizon favors steady profit over costly escalation.
B has held at 10, and A joined at 10 last round. Matching 10 preserves a share if they hold; a higher wage risks reducing profit without clear evidence of a rival move.
B has held at 10 throughout; matching earns a reliable share while avoiding unnecessary wage cuts. C’s one undercut failed to win labor against B and A at 10.
All rivals have repeatedly bid 10. Matching preserves a profitable share; bidding higher sacrifices profit per unit without evidence it is needed.
Rivals have repeatedly held at 10; matching preserves a chance at a share while avoiding an undercut that earns less if they stay tied.
Matching 10 has been the reliable choice: B matches, and C’s undercut has earned no labor. A higher offer would sacrifice profit without evidence it would win more labor.
Bidding 10 has repeatedly secured a profitable share; bidding higher cuts margin, while bidding lower risks losing the labor.
At 10, I share the unit with both rivals for profit 3.33. Undercutting by one only helps if both rivals stay at 10, while risking another round with no labor; matching is the steadier choice.
